back: An early investigation deciding whether a proposed system is possible, practical and worthwhile; ends in a recommendation.
Can it be built and run with available hardware, software, power, network and skills?
Do the benefits (savings, extra income) outweigh development and running costs?
Does it obey laws: data protection, copyright and licences, tax, employment?
Will the system work in practice: can and will the users use it, and does it fit how the organisation works?
Social: effect on jobs, workers and the community. Schedule: can it be completed in the time available?
Payback = development cost ÷ (yearly saving − yearly running cost).
Tangible: measurable in money (saved wages, less waste). Intangible: hard to measure (customer satisfaction, reputation).
States whether to proceed and which option, justified by findings in each area, with any conditions.
